report:
**Conclusion:** High-quality scientific evidence shows that **ivermectin does not lower the risk of death** or improve key clinical outcomes in COVID-19 patients.

### Key Evidence Summary

1. **Large Clinical Trials:** High-quality randomized controlled trials (such as the TOGETHER and ACTIV-6 trials) evaluated ivermectin in thousands of patients. Findings published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* showed that ivermectin did not reduce mortality, hospitalizations, or emergency room visits compared to a placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869).

2. **Systematic Reviews:** A systematic review by the Cochrane Collaboration concluded that there is no high-quality evidence supporting ivermectin for preventing or treating COVID-19. Initial interest stemmed from laboratory cell-culture studies, but achieving similar antiviral effects in humans would require doses far above safe toxicological limits (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD015017_ivermectin-preventing-and-treating-covid-19).

3. **Health Agency Recommendations:** Major health and regulatory bodies—including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), National Institutes of Health (NIH), and World Health Organization (WHO)—recommend against using ivermectin to prevent or treat COVID-19 outside of clinical trials due to lack of efficacy and potential risk of adverse events (https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/ivermectin-and-covid-19; https://www.journalofinfection.com/article/S0163-4453(24)00064-1/fulltext).

In summary, clinical trials consistently demonstrate that ivermectin provides no mortality benefit for COVID-19.
